In the matter of Arihant Retail Private Limited 
 
 
Regulation 39(4) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India 
(Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporat e Persons) Regulations, 
2016 (CIRP Regulations, 2016) by the Resolution Professional of the 
Corporate Debtor viz.,  ARIHANT RETAIL PRIVATE LIMITED seeking 
approval of resolution plan submitted by the Successful Resolution 
Applicant (SRA) viz., POTHYS RETAIL PRIVATE LIMITED seeking the 
following reliefs:  
A. Allow the present application; 
B. Approve the Resolution Plan dated 27.02.2026 & addendum dated 
20.07.2026 submitted by the Pothys Retail Pvt.  Ltd, (SRA), as 
approved by the Committee of Creditors of the Corporate Debtor, 
Arihant Retail Private Limited, with 100% voting share in favour 
under Section 30(4) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, 
after considering its feasibility and viability in terms of Section 31 of 
the Code. 
C. Grant and allow the reliefs, concessions, and waivers, sought under 
Clause 26 (Page 48 to 55 of the Resolution plan dated 27.02.2026) of 
the Resolution plan dated 27.02.2026  to the extent deemed fit and 
proper by this Tribunal. 
D. In terms of the Resolution Plan, direct for the appointment of the 
Monitoring Committee.  
E. To pass such further orders/reliefs as may be deemed fit and proper 
in the facts and circumstances of the case and thus render justice.

3. SALIENT FEATURES OF THE RESOLUTION PLAN 
3.1. The Successful Resolution Applicant (SRA) is Pothys Retail 
Private Limited, having its registered office at Pothys Traditional 
Showroom, No.15. Nageswara Rao Road. T. Nagar Thygarayanagar, 
Chennai 600017 . The SRA is part of the Pothys Group which is a 
reputed business group with a long -standing presence in Indian textile 
and retail sector. As of the year ended 3 1.03.2025, the Pothys Group 
has cloaked a turnover of Rs. 6000 Crores (US$700 million) with net 
positive margin. SRA affirms that it has examined the business of the 
Corporate Debtor and is satisfied that the Corporate Debtor can be 
revived through the implementation of the Resolution Plan.  
3.2. Chapter I Clause 2  of the Plan define s, ‘Approval Date’  as the 
date on which the Adjudicating Authority approves  the Resolution 
Plan.  ‘Effective Date’  is defined as the date on which this resolution 
plan is finally approved by the Adjudicating Authority vide its order 
of approval, subject to there being no stay/ injunction being granted by 
any court/tribunal with respect to the NCLT Approval Order and/o r 
the implementation of this Resolution Plan.

4.2. CIRP Costs: 
a. The CIRP costs shall be paid in  actuals in full and in priority to 
the payment of any other debts or  claims of the Corporate Debtor, in 
accordance with the provisions of the IBC, 2016.  
b. As per  the Addendum to the Plan, the estimated CIRP costs is 
Rs. 65,00,000/- (Rupees Sixty-Five Lakhs). The SRA in the Addendum  
proposes to pay Rs. 65,00,000/- (Rupees Sixty-Five Lakhs) towards 
CIRP costs.  
c. If the CIRP costs exceed the estimated amount under the Plan, 
additional CIRP costs will be paid by the SRA.  
d. If the actual CIRP  costs is less than the estimated CIRP costs, 
remaining surplus shall be paid to the Secured Financial Creditors in 
proportion to their respective entitlements under the Plan. 
4.3. Financial Creditors:  
a. The Substituted Clause 10.2 of the Addendum to the Resolution 
Plan provides for payment of  Rs. 42,25,00,000 (Rupees Forty-Two 
Crores Twenty-Five Lakhs Only) toward  full and final settlement of 
claims of the Secured Financial Creditors.  
b. The Addendum provides the CoC with the liberty to approve, 
modify or adopt the inter se distribution of the Plan proceeds amongst 
the Secured Financial Creditors.
